<description>
SignPSBTInput() checked existing signatures against an assumed sighash type when neither PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE nor the sighashtype parameter was given: SIGHASH_DEFAULT for taproot, SIGHASH_ALL otherwise. A PSBT holding a valid 65-byte SIGHASH_ALL taproot signature could then be neither finalized nor signed further.

BIP 174 lets a signer use any sighash type when the field is absent, so the check now runs only when the field or the parameter is given, for every input type. Without the field, RemoveUnnecessaryTransactions() now also looks at the taproot signatures for SIGHASH_ANYONECANPAY, so that the non_witness_utxo is kept. A functional test in rpc_psbt.py covers a taproot input signed with ALL, NONE and ALL|ANYONECANPAY without the field. A second commit also keeps the non_witness_utxo of a finalized taproot input, whose signatures are left only in the final witness, and tests it on a key path and a script path.

Fixes #36507.
</description>

<new_statements>
[2026-11-05] rc:4487236951 inline on src/psbt.cpp by fametrano (contributor):
Done: existing signatures' sighash types are now checked only when PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE or the sighashtype parameter is given. Without either, any type is accepted, on non-taproot inputs too, as BIP 174 allows. As you suggest, this replaces the rule I argued for on #36558, which accepted only ALL besides DEFAULT. RemoveUnnecessaryTransactions also finds ANYONECANPAY in taproot signatures. The unit tests became a functional test.
[2026-11-05] c:6672727025 comment by fametrano (contributor):
Once a taproot input is finalized, its sighash type field and its taproot signatures are no longer serialized, so a later `utxoupdatepsbt` or `walletprocesspsbt` drops its non_witness_utxo even when it was signed with ANYONECANPAY. The second commit also reads the signatures in the final witness, through the same check as the first commit.
</new_statements>
